# Description

First step of #3724, reworked after review: instead of a dedicated `RMSNormGated` op, this adds a small `SiLUGate` basic op, so gated RMSNorm is

    te_ops.Sequential(te_ops.RMSNorm(hidden_size), te_ops.SiLUGate())

`SiLUGate` takes the gate as an extra input and computes `y = x * silu(gate)`. The SiLU part is computed in FP32; `y` and `dx` are returned in the input dtype and `dgate` in the gate's dtype. Output quantization isn't supported, so it returns an unquantized tensor and the next op quantizes. A fused norm+gate kernel can come later as a fused op that only covers the cases the kernel supports.

Refs #3724, NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#6757

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change (change only to the documentation, either a fix or a new content)
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring

## Changes

- `transformer_engine/pytorch/ops/basic/silu_gate.py`: new `SiLUGate` basic op with one extra input (the gate).
- Export it from `transformer_engine.pytorch.ops` and add it to the API docs.
- `tests/pytorch/test_fusible_ops.py`:
  - `test_silu_gate` checks y, dx and dgate against a reference for each dtype and two shapes.
  - `test_rmsnorm_silu_gate` checks `Sequential(RMSNorm, SiLUGate)` end to end (y, dx, dweight, dgate), with zero-centered gamma on and off. The reference rounds the normalized output and its gradient to the input dtype like the op chain does, instead of loosening tolerances.

Tested on an RTX 3090 (SM86), torch 2.13.0+cu130:

    python -m pytest -q tests/pytorch/test_fusible_ops.py -k "silu_gate or rmsnorm"   # 96 passed

I haven't run it on Hopper/Blackwell yet.

AI assistance: I used Claude Code to help write the code and tests. I reviewed the change, ran the validation above on my own GPU, and I'll handle the review.

- [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)

- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works

nodes.body: Thanks, that's cleaner. I replaced `RMSNormGated` with a `SiLUGate` basic op (gate as an extra input), so the gated norm is now `Sequential(RMSNorm(...), SiLUGate())`. Tests cover the op alone and the RMSNorm + SiLUGate chain. A fused kernel would come later as a fused op, as you suggested.

@timmoon10 when you have time, could you take another look? This is now just the `SiLUGate` basic op (gate as an extra input), with gated RMSNorm expressed as `Sequential(RMSNorm(...), SiLUGate())`, as you suggested.

Confidence Score: 4/5

**[Medium impact]** The change reaches PyTorch callers who use the operation fuser\. Fix the BF16 reference calculation before merging so correct operation results do not fail the new tests.

Findings

1.  **BF16 reference skips rounding** ▶

Summary

Adds `SiLUGate` for `y = x * silu(gate)` and exposes it through the public API. - PyTorch callers can multiply an input by the SiLU of a separate gate. Reviews (5) · Last reviewed commit: ["Merge branch 'main' into feat/rmsnorm-ga..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/05ce561e1763e9d6f1fe62601332570f10aa39d1) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

@timmoon10 could you take another look when you have time? The PR now adds only the SiLUGate basic op, with gated RMSNorm composed as Sequential(RMSNorm(...), SiLUGate()), as you suggested. The latest commit also adds negative-gate coverage. Please let me know if anything else is needed for the re-review.

@timmoon10 Thanks for the LGTM. The three `L0_pytorch_unittest` jobs (A100, H100, B200) are failing, but the logs aren't visible from outside NVIDIA. Could you tell me which tests fail, or share the relevant part of the log? If they're in `test_fusible_ops.py` or the norm tests, I'll fix them right away. If they're unrelated, could you rerun `/te-ci`?

This seems like a rather large and bespoke operation to treat as a first-class citizen. How about we separate the RMSNorm and gate logic by just implementing a `SiLUGate` basic op? Then you can reproduce this function with `Sequential(RMSNorm(...), SiLUGate())`. You can easily change to a different norm or a different gating function (if we add more in the future).

Once you have a fused kernel, the right design is to expose it in a fused op. This has several advantages:
- Your fused kernel doesn't need to be fully general. Only enable the fusion for the cases that the kernel supports, and in other cases we fallback to the unfused impl.
- If you only fuse the forward pass or only fuse the backward pass, your implementation only needs to consider that case.

**Negative gates lack coverage** Both new tests draw gates from the default range `[0, 1)`, so neither checks the negative side of SiLU. This matters because `silu_grad` changes sign for negative gates, but stays positive throughout the tested range. A mistake there could pass both tests and change how a model learns. Add signed gate values, including values near `-1.28` and larger negative magnitudes, and compare both gradients with PyTorch. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

# Description

First step of #3724, reworked after review: instead of a dedicated `RMSNormGated` op, this adds a small `SiLUGate` basic op, so gated RMSNorm is

    te_ops.Sequential(te_ops.RMSNorm(hidden_size), te_ops.SiLUGate())

`SiLUGate` takes the gate as an extra input and computes `y = x * silu(gate)`. The SiLU part is computed in FP32; `y` and `dx` are returned in the input dtype and `dgate` in the gate's dtype. Output quantization isn't supported, so it returns an unquantized tensor and the next op quantizes. A fused norm+gate kernel can come later as a fused op that only covers the cases the kernel supports.

Refs #3724, NVIDIA/Megatron-LM#6757

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change (change only to the documentation, either a fix or a new content)
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring

## Changes

- `transformer_engine/pytorch/ops/basic/silu_gate.py`: new `SiLUGate` basic op with one extra input (the gate).
- Export it from `transformer_engine.pytorch.ops` and add it to the API docs.
- `tests/pytorch/test_fusible_ops.py`:
  - `test_silu_gate` checks y, dx and dgate against a reference for each dtype and two shapes.
  - `test_rmsnorm_silu_gate` checks `Sequential(RMSNorm, SiLUGate)` end to end (y, dx, dweight, dgate), with zero-centered gamma on and off. The reference rounds the normalized output and its gradient to the input dtype like the op chain does, instead of loosening tolerances.

Tested on an RTX 3090 (SM86), torch 2.13.0+cu130:

    python -m pytest -q tests/pytorch/test_fusible_ops.py -k "silu_gate or rmsnorm"   # 96 passed

I haven't run it on Hopper/Blackwell yet.

+"""Fusable operation for SiLU gating."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence
+from typing import Any, Optional
+
+import torch
+
+from ...cpu_offload import is_cpu_offload_enabled, mark_activation_offload
+from ...tensor import Quantizer
+from ..op import BasicOperation, OperationContext
+from .._common import maybe_autocast_dtype, maybe_dequantize
+
+
+class SiLUGate(BasicOperation):
+    r"""Multiply input by the SiLU activation of a gate tensor
+
+    This operation takes the main input :math:`x` and an extra gate
+    tensor :math:`g` and computes
+
+    .. math::
+        y = x * \mathrm{SiLU}(g) = \frac{x g}{1 + \exp(-g)}
+
+    The gate tensor is an extra operation input and must have the same
+    shape as the main input. Computation is performed in FP32 and the
+    output is returned in the input dtype.
+
+    This operation is typically used after a normalization operation to
+    implement gated RMSNorm, as in Mamba2 and Qwen3-Next:
+
+    .. code-block:: python
+
+        op = Sequential(RMSNorm(hidden_size), SiLUGate())
+
+    Output quantization is not supported.
+
+    """
+
+    num_extra_inputs: int = 1
+
+    def fuser_forward(
+        self,
+        basic_op_ctxs: list[OperationContext],
+        input_: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        basic_op_extra_inputs: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]],
+        prev_op_grad_output_quantizer: Optional[Quantizer],
+        next_op_input_quantizer: Optional[Quantizer],
+        basic_op_kwargs: list[dict[str, Any]],
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, Sequence[Sequence[torch.Tensor]]]:
+        # Output quantization is not supported. Return an unquantized
+        # tensor and leave quantization to the next operation.
+        del prev_op_grad_output_quantizer, next_op_input_quantizer, basic_op_kwargs
+
+        # Check input tensors
+        x = maybe_dequantize(input_.contiguous())
+        gate = maybe_dequantize(basic_op_extra_inputs[0][0].contiguous())
+        if gate.shape != x.shape:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Input tensor (shape={tuple(x.shape)}) "
+                f"and gate tensor (shape={tuple(gate.shape)}) are not compatible"
+            )
+        dtype = maybe_autocast_dtype(default_dtype=x.dtype)
+        x = maybe_dequantize(x, dtype)
+
+        # Compute SiLU gate in FP32
+        y = (x.float() * torch.nn.functional.silu(gate.float())).to(dtype)
+
+        # Save state for backward pass
+        ctx = basic_op_ctxs[0]
+        if ctx.requires_grad:
+            if is_cpu_offload_enabled():
+                mark_activation_offload(x, gate)
+            ctx.save_for_backward(x, gate)
+
+        return y, [()]
+
+    def fuser_backward(
+        self,
+        basic_op_ctxs: list[OperationContext],
+        grad_output: torch.Tensor,
+        *,
+        basic_op_grad_extra_outputs: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]],
+    ) -> tuple[
+        torch.Tensor,
+        Iterable[Iterable[Optional[torch.Tensor]]],
+        Iterable[Iterable[Optional[torch.Tensor]]],
+    ]:
+        del basic_op_grad_extra_outputs
+
+        # Saved tensors from forward pass
+        ctx = basic_op_ctxs[0]
+        x, gate = ctx.saved_tensors
+
+        dy = maybe_dequantize(grad_output.contiguous(), x.dtype)
+
+        # Gradients of the SiLU gate, computed in FP32
+        x_fp32 = x.float()
+        gate_fp32 = gate.float()
+        dy_fp32 = dy.float()
+        sigmoid = torch.sigmoid(gate_fp32)
+        silu_grad = sigmoid * (1 + gate_fp32 * (1 - sigmoid))
+        dx = (dy_fp32 * torch.nn.functional.silu(gate_fp32)).to(x.dtype)
+        dgate = (dy_fp32 * x_fp32 * silu_grad).to(gate.dtype)
+

reviews.body:
This seems like a rather large and bespoke operation to treat as a first-class citizen. How about we separate the RMSNorm and gate logic by just implementing a `SiLUGate` basic op? Then you can reproduce this function with `Sequential(RMSNorm(...), SiLUGate())`. You can easily change to a different norm or a different gating function (if we add more in the future).

Once you have a fused kernel, the right design is to expose it in a fused op. This has several advantages:
- Your fused kernel doesn't need to be fully general. Only enable the fusion for the cases that the kernel supports, and in other cases we fallback to the unfused impl.
- If you only fuse the forward pass or only fuse the backward pass, your implementation only needs to consider that case.
